subject: TempoPay: activation latency expectations & scale checklist
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Diane Park <diane@tempopay.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: TempoPay SLOs / post-call notes — activation latency & streaming

Hi Diane + Aisha — thanks for the time today. Quick recap from my side with concrete asks so we can scope a focused scale test: 

Summary of TempoPay targets we heard today:
- P99 end-to-end streaming latency: "<= 450ms per first partial-stream chunk" for 512-token responses
- Sustained throughput target: 120 concurrent streaming connections per deployment region
- Peak burst tolerance: absorb a 3x concurrency spike for up to 45s without exceeding 800ms P95
- Desired cold-start scale-up: provide extra instances to achieve 80% of target within 60s (warm-pool preferred)

Unknowns / clarifying items we need from you to design the test:
1) Typical request size distribution (median/95th token lengths).
2) Are there per-customer routing constraints (region pinning) or single global endpoint?
3) Any client-side retry behavior we should simulate (backoff, max retries)?

Proposed immediate next steps:
- TempoPay shares a small sample of traffic traces (anonymized) and confirmation of request sizes. (see our suggested template attached)
- Redwood builds a targeted scale test that simulates steady-state plus a 3x ramp burst and measures per-chunk streaming latency, KV cache hit variation, and queueing time.
- Run test in a staging window (we propose Wed 09/30 10:00–11:30 PT).

Attachment: scale-test-plan.xlsx (sheet: test-cases, payload-sizes) — this is a working draft we can adapt.

Thanks — I can run test planning with Aisha & Marissa and then share a checklist for the test window.

Best,
Aditya
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

From: Diane Park <diane@tempopay.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 16:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: TempoPay SLOs / post-call notes — activation latency & streaming

Thanks Aditya — that looks right. Quick clarifications from our side:
- Median response length: ~140 tokens; 95th: ~540 tokens. We mostly stream, first partial chunk is emitted after model starts token generation.
- We operate two active regions (us-west, us-east). We prefer region-local routing for latency reasons.
- Client behavior: simple retry with exponential backoff, but a single retry only (no aggressive replays).

We can provide a 24-hour anonymized trace slice and a short doc that maps request IDs to token counts — attaching now.

We can also confirm the Wed 09/30 10:00–11:30 PT window for the test. Please ensure the test simulates the farmed-down behavior (i.e., clients that start but then drop before full response) — we see this often in mobile flows and it impacts early-chunk latency.

Regards,
Diane Park
Head of Platform, TempoPay
diane@tempopay.com

Attachment: tempo_trace_slice.json (referenced; we sent via secure link)

Thanks for the trace, Diane — that helps a lot. Planning note and mutual action plan below.

Planned test scope (Redwood):
- Target region: us-west (primary) with a follow-up run in us-east if we spot region-specific variance.
- Test phases: baseline ramp (to 120 concurrent streams), sustained (5m), 3x burst (sustained 45s), cooldown.
- Metrics recorded: per-chunk latency (first chunk + subsequent chunks), per-request queue time, instance boot time, KV cache hit rate, per-instance CPU/GPU utilization.

Mutual action plan / timeline:
- Today (Tue): Redwood will finalize test scripts and share the exact traffic template (we updated the attached "scale-test-plan.xlsx").
- Wed 09/30 10:00 PT: Execute primary scale test in staging (Monitoring + live metrics stream provided).
- Thu 10/01: Redwood to deliver test report with a short recommendation list (warm-pool sizing, scale-up target, queueing thresholds).

A few specific asks for test fidelity (Diane):
- Confirm 95th token length mapping is included in the trace.
- Indicate any IP ranges or headers we should preserve for regional routing.

Attachments: scale-test-plan.xlsx (updated), slo-definition.pdf (TempoPay target summary)

If that timeline works, we will: (1) lock the Wed slot, (2) run a short smoke test 30 minutes before the window, (3) share the live dashboard link.

Best,
Aisha Rahman

Quick internal note before we run: a few operational items to keep in mind during the window — copying here so Diane sees the final schedule when Aisha hits send:

Operational checklist:
- Warm pool: provision 4 pre-warmed instances in us-west (configured for KV-cache priming).
- Autoscaler tuning: set target ramp policy to add up to 2 instances per 15s; allow burst policy to bypass scale-down for 90s post-burst.
- Queueing: enable temporary request queuing with a 10s cap; observe queue drain profile in the first 60s after burst.
- Streaming: ensure partial-chunk flush threshold is consistent across instances (we've seen edge cases where first-chunk batching introduces 100–150ms jitter).

I'll be on the call for the smoke test at 09:30 PT and the main run at 10:00 PT. Aisha — please confirm you want me to post the live dashboard link to the TempoPay channel once the run starts.

-Marissa
